hypothesis: Rather than proposing yet another feature/architecture guess to chase noise-sized deltas, directly attack the noise itself: train the current-best bilinear BPR-FM mechanism as a small bag of independently-seeded models (different init + different per-epoch negative draws) and average their raw logits before evaluation. This is classic bagging variance-reduction, distinct from the "ensembling" lever's past failures (which combined two *architecturally different but highly correlated* single runs) — here the diversity source is training stochasticity in the exact same accepted-best mechanism, which should genuinely decorrelate the ranking errors that dominate the noise floor identified in probe node 13.
reflection: The pos_bucket fatigue feature actually made things slightly worse and overfit (peaked epoch 4, degraded by epoch 8) — the metric-noise probe (node 13, primary bootstrap std ~0.0017, p5-p95 range ~0.0055) suggests this loss, like several previous "rejections," may partly reflect training-run noise rather than a genuinely worse mechanism. Nine iterations of single-seed point-estimates chasing sub-0.005 deltas is consistent with us fighting noise, not signal.
expected_effect: nDCG@5 should move more than GAUC, because probe node 13 found nDCG@5's bootstrap std (0.00264) exceeds GAUC's (0.00229) and 55% of valid users have <5 rows where per-model score noise most easily flips a top-5 ordering — averaging independently-trained models should smooth exactly this small-candidate-set instability the most.
